best_parts: node predict_site: the two TR1 distractors split the depth model ('the deeper, more sheltered site') from the artery-danger model; each gets tempting-then-refute feedback and its own sure_note
node why_h1 and why_h2: the thin-wall trap and the reversed-mechanism trap are distinct wrong models, each refuted with the anatomy of what lies behind the wall, then re-tested in a second form
node predict_reaction and pr_h2: the gastritis trap is a different wrong model from the recovery trap (cause versus direction), and pr_w2 refutes it with the definition of a full-wall perforation
flaws: node predict_site: the key is the longest option and carries the mechanism clause ('which faces the free peritoneal cavity'), so it is findable by form (DP1)
node lie_probe: the key 'Movement jars the inflamed peritoneum and worsens the pain' is the only option naming movement as the mechanism; the colic trap is shorter (DP1)
node site_w1, pr_w1, lie_w1: 'Show me why' restates the explanation already given rather than using a different technique such as a contrast or case (R5)

best_parts: node cases_t1 and cases_t2: 'depth sounds like danger' and 'the splenic artery is a familiar name' each name the tempting model before the refutation, and the artery trap is a clean artery-swap
node stages_t1 and stages_t2: two distinct TR17 errors (bacteria first; reaction last), each with a sure_note naming what the learner was assuming
node tissue_t2: 'pain severity drives movement' is a separate wrong model from the colic trap, refuted by the mechanism of movement on inflamed peritoneum
flaws: node cases: the stem's symptoms (A rigid with free gas, B haematemesis and melaena) answer 'which is the posterior ulcer' before any anatomy is used, so the probe tests symptom-reading; 'Patient B' appears in the key and in one trap, so the key is findable by form (DP1)
node cases_t1, cases_t2, stages_t1, stages_t2, tissue_t1, tissue_t2: the only route after a miss is 'Try again' to the same question; there is no agency, no second explanation (R5)
node cases_ok: the commonest-site claim K1 is never stated in S2, so the commonest-site part of O1 is not taught on this path (R3)

best_parts: node c_t2: 'discharge on a PPI tonight' is refuted as a sealing model, separate from c_t1's recovery model, so the path separates two different wrong beliefs about the same calm
node h_t1 and h_t2: the colic-gut-wall trap and the pain-severity trap each get a mechanism refutation citing K27, with a distinct wrong model behind each
node w1 and w2: the worked patient A, step by step with the period of reaction named, gives a full timeline that the later probes can use
flaws: node open and g: one trap each (open offers only the back-wall ulcer, g only the rolling patient), so these probes cannot separate models beyond a near coin flip (R2)
node c_t1, c_t2, g_t, d_t1, b_t1: no agency or second explanation; every miss returns to the same question (R5)
node d: the sequence probe has no hint option and no ask_confidence, unlike the other probes in the segment (R2, R5)

merge_ideas: a's predict_site and why_probe structure with c's w1/w2 worked patient A as the second explanation after a repeated miss, so the remediation uses a different technique rather than a restatement
c's c_t2 sealing trap added to a's predict_reaction as a third distractor, so the reaction probe separates recovery, gastritis and sealing as three different wrong models

b's cases stem with the symptoms withheld from the key clause (both patients described by the same feature set) as a second-form re-test of the wall-to-outcome pairing, so the key is not findable by symptom-matching
a's lie_probe key length equalised with its traps, plus c's g probe as a fast-lane pre-check for the stillness sign
